# Intear API

> Prices, token data, charts, trades, transfers and balances for NEAR fungible tokens, live over one WebSocket.

The Intear API has prices, token data, charts, trades, transfers, balances and holders for every fungible token on NEAR. All of it comes live over one WebSocket, updated after every block, and the parts that answer once are plain HTTP too.

```
wss://api.intea.rs/ws
https://api.intea.rs
```

It's built for apps that show token data:
- You ask for only the fields you show, so responses stay small.
- Updates can come after every block, or only once a value has moved by a threshold you pick.
- History and live updates join up exactly, so a list of trades never misses or repeats one.

:::note
No API key is needed. Every message reports the [credits](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/limits.md#credits) it would cost, but nothing is charged yet.
:::

## What you can do

- **Token lists**: Every token's price, liquidity, volume, supply and more, filtered and sorted, kept live with [`tokens.subscribe`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/tokens.md#tokenssubscribe).
- **Charts**: Candles in USD or NEAR, from 1 second to 1 week, with the latest candle updated live. See [`candles`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/candles.md).
- **Trades and transfers**: Every swap, transfer and transaction, as history and then live, filtered by token, account or size.
- **Wallets**: An account's balances, its activity across trades and transfers, and every token's top holders.

## Conventions

- Tokens are identified by their contract's account ID, like `wrap.near`.
- Amounts in a token's smallest units (balances, supplies, trade amounts) are decimal strings, since they don't fit in a JSON number.
- `price_usd` is USD per whole token. `price_usd_raw` is the unscaled form the indexer works in: `price_usd = price_usd_raw × 10^(decimals − 6)`.
- Prices and USD values sent as strings have at most 30 significant digits and no trailing zeros. A token without a price has `"0"`.
- `*_millis` are Unix timestamps in milliseconds, and `height` is a NEAR block height.
- In trades, native NEAR is always `wrap.near`. In balances and transfers it's `near`, in yoctoNEAR.

## Next steps

- [Quickstart](https://docs.intear.tech/api/quickstart.md): Fetch tokens over HTTP, then keep a live token list over the WebSocket.

- [Token fields](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/token-fields.md): Every field a token has, and what it can be filtered and sorted by.

## Replaced APIs

The Intear API replaces the Events API (`wss://ws-events-v3.intear.tech`, `https://events-v3.intear.tech`) and the prices API, also called the Token Indexer (`https://prices.intear.tech`). Write new code against the Intear API. For code that uses the old ones:

| Before | Now |
| --- | --- |
| `trade_swap` events, and `/v3/trade_swap/*` | [`trades.subscribe`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/trades.md#tradessubscribe) and [`trades.query`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/trades.md#tradesquery) |
| `ft_transfer` events | [`transfers.subscribe` and `transfers.query`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/transfers.md) |
| `price_token` events, and `/v3/price_token/latest_price` | `price_usd` in [`tokens.subscribe`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/tokens.md#tokenssubscribe) and [`tokens.get`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/tokens.md#tokensget) |
| `/v3/price_token/ohlc` and `/v3/price_token/price_at_time` | [`candles.get`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/candles.md#candlesget) and [`prices.at`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/prices.md#pricesat) |
| `newtoken_nep141` events | A [`tokens.subscribe`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/tokens.md#tokenssubscribe) list sorted by `created_at`, where a new token comes with all of its fields |
| `/tokens`, `/token`, `/prices`, `/price` and the other price endpoints | [`tokens.get`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/tokens.md#tokensget), with only the [fields](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/token-fields.md) you need |
| `/token-search` | [`tokens.search`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/tokens.md#tokenssearch) |
| The reputation lists, like `/tokens-reputable` and `/token-spam-list` | The `reputation` field of [tokens](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/token-fields.md) |
| `chart.intear.tech` | [Charts](https://docs.intear.tech/api/guides/charts.md), with a [TradingView example](https://docs.intear.tech/api/guides/charts.md#example-tradingview) |

The Events API's other events, like the NFT, Potlock and SocialDB ones, have no counterpart: the Intear API is about fungible tokens.

## For agents

Every page is also Markdown, at its URL with `.md` in place of the trailing slash, like [`/api/reference/tokens.md`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/tokens.md), or at its URL itself for a request with `Accept: text/markdown`. [`/api/llms-full.txt`](https://docs.intear.tech/api/llms-full.txt) has all the Intear API pages in one file, and [`/llms.txt`](https://docs.intear.tech/llms.txt) lists every page of these docs.

The [`intear-api` skill](https://docs.intear.tech/skills/intear-api/SKILL.md) has the endpoints and rules of the Intear API for agents. To install it, save it as `intear-api/SKILL.md` in the agent's skills folder, like `~/.claude/skills/` for Claude Code.

# Quickstart

> Fetch tokens over HTTP, then keep a live token list over the WebSocket.

The examples use `fetch` and the browser's `WebSocket`, which Node.js has too.

## Over HTTP

1. **Ask for tokens, with only the fields you need.**

   ```
   GET https://api.intea.rs/tokens?ids=wrap.near&fields=symbol,price_usd
   ```

   ```json
   {
     "height": 219969220,
     "timestamp_millis": 1792003477277,
     "columns": ["account_id", "symbol", "price_usd"],
     "rows": [["wrap.near", "wNEAR", "4.815189744118901"]],
     "total": 1,
     "missing": []
   }
   ```

   Tokens come as a [table](https://docs.intear.tech/api/guides/connecting.md#tables): the column names once, then a row per token, in the same order. `account_id` always comes first.

2. **Turn the table into objects, if that's easier to work with.**

   ```js
   /**
    * Turns a table into `{ <key>: { <column>: value } }`, keyed by its first column
    */
   function tableToObjects({ columns, rows }) {
     const objects = {};
     for (const row of rows) {
       const object = {};
       columns.slice(1).forEach((column, i) => (object[column] = row[i + 1]));
       objects[String(row[0])] = object;
     }
     return objects;
   }

   const params = new URLSearchParams({
     ids: 'wrap.near,usdt.tether-token.near',
     fields: 'symbol,price_usd,liquidity_usd,price_change_24h',
   });
   const response = await fetch(`https://api.intea.rs/tokens?${params}`);
   const result = await response.json();
   if (!response.ok) throw new Error(result.error.message);
   const tokens = tableToObjects(result);
   // tokens['wrap.near'] is { symbol: 'wNEAR', price_usd: '4.81', ... }
   ```

   The whole file, tested in CI: https://docs.intear.tech/snippets/js/src/intear-api.js

Every method that answers once, except `tokens.update` and `unsubscribe`, works like this over HTTP. See [Using HTTP](https://docs.intear.tech/api/guides/http.md) for how params go in a URL.

## Over the WebSocket

1. **Connect.** The server's first message is a `hello`, with the latest block and the [limits](https://docs.intear.tech/api/reference/limits.md):

   ```json
   { "hello": { "version": 2, "height": 219969289, "timestamp_millis": 1792003517185, "limits": { ... } }, "credits_used": 0 }
   ```

2. **Subscribe.** Send a request with an `id` you choose. The reply has the same `id`, and every update after it has `sub` set to that `id`:

   ```json
   → { "id": 1, "method": "tokens.subscribe", "params": { "fields": ["symbol", "price_usd"], "ids": ["wrap.near"] } }
   ← { "id": 1, "result": { "height": 219969289, "columns": ["account_id", "symbol", "price_usd"], "rows": [["wrap.near", "wNEAR", "4.81"]], ... } }
   ← { "sub": 1, "height": 219969292, "set": { "wrap.near": { "price_usd": "4.82" } }, ... }
   ```

   Updates only carry what changed: here, only `price_usd` of `wrap.near`.

3. **Keep a list up to date.** This follows the 20 `NotFake` or `Reputable` tokens with the most volume in the last 24 hours. Prices only update once they've moved 0.1%, and tokens that drop out of the top 20 are in `left`:

   The examples on this site use this small client. It matches replies to requests by `id`, and passes each subscription's updates to its callback:

   ```js
   /** A minimal Intear API client: requests resolve with their result, and pushes go to their subscription's callback */
   export class IntearApi {
     #socket;
     #nextId = 1;
     #pending = new Map();
     #subscriptions = new Map();
     ready;

     constructor(url = 'wss://api.intea.rs/ws') {
       this.#socket = new WebSocket(url);
       this.ready = new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
         this.#socket.addEventListener('error', () => reject(new Error('Connection failed')));
         this.#socket.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
           const message = JSON.parse(event.data);
           if ('hello' in message) {
             resolve(message.hello);
           } else if ('sub' in message) {
             this.#subscriptions.get(message.sub)?.(message);
           } else if ('id' in message) {
             const request = this.#pending.get(message.id);
             this.#pending.delete(message.id);
             if ('error' in message) {
               this.#subscriptions.delete(message.id);
               const error = message.error;
               request?.reject(new Error(`${error.code}: ${error.message}`));
             } else {
               request?.resolve(message.result);
             }
           }
         });
       });
     }

     /**
      * Sends a request, and resolves with its result
      */
     async request(method, params) {
       await this.ready;
       const id = this.#nextId++;
       const result = new Promise((resolve, reject) => this.#pending.set(id, { resolve, reject }));
       this.#socket.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));
       return result;
     }

     /**
      * Makes a subscription. `onPush` gets each of its pushes, after the result
      */
     async subscribe(method, params, onPush) {
       await this.ready;
       const id = this.#nextId++;
       this.#subscriptions.set(id, onPush);
       const result = new Promise((resolve, reject) => this.#pending.set(id, { resolve, reject }));
       this.#socket.send(JSON.stringify({ id, method, params }));
       return { sub: id, result: await result };
     }

     async unsubscribe(sub) {
       await this.request('unsubscribe', { sub });
       this.#subscriptions.delete(sub);
     }

     close() {
       this.#socket.close();
     }
   }
   ```

   The whole file, tested in CI: https://docs.intear.tech/snippets/js/src/intear-api.js

   ```js
   const tokens = new Map();

   const { result } = await api.subscribe(
     'tokens.subscribe',
     {
       fields: ['symbol', 'icon_hash', 'price_usd', 'volume_usd_24h'],
       where: { min_reputation: 'NotFake' },
       sort: { by: 'volume_usd_24h', desc: true },
       limit: 20,
       min_change: { price_usd: '0.1%', volume_usd_24h: '1%' },
       precision: 6,
     },
     (push) => {
       if (push.end) throw new Error(`Subscription ended: ${push.end.message}`);
       for (const [token, fields] of Object.entries(push.set ?? {})) {
         tokens.set(token, { ...tokens.get(token), ...fields });
       }
       for (const token of push.left ?? []) tokens.delete(token);
       render(tokens);
     },
   );

   for (const [token, fields] of Object.entries(tableToObjects(result))) tokens.set(token, fields);
   render(tokens);
   ```

   The whole file, tested in CI: https://docs.intear.tech/snippets/js/src/intear-api.js
